image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Choropleth map** of U.S. counties.

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses a **geographic map layout** with counties as the unit of analysis.
- Includes **inset maps** for **Alaska** and **Hawaii**.
- No faceting, stacking, or small multiples.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| U.S. county location | Geographic/spatial | Position on map |
| Number of local news outlets (binned: None, 1, 2–5, 6–9, 10+) | Ordinal | Color/hue of county fill |
| State name/abbreviation | Categorical/nominal | Text labels on map |
| Selected county/state callout statistics (e.g., California 524, L.A. County 104, NYC metro lost 210, Texas 29 counties with none) | Quantitative | Annotation text/callouts with leader lines |

comments.raw_comment:
I notice that California has the most local news outlets, a great portion of these outlets are located in Los Angeles. This makes sense as California, L.A. more specifically, is filled with millions of celebrities, and with this high celebrity presence comes a desire to hear about their life and drama. Celebrity gossip often appears on news channels and outlets. L.A. itself is also a bustling city with a lot going on such as big businesses, movie and tv production, as well as real estate. There is therefore a lot of news to capture and document. I wonder why New York has suffered such a decline in news outlets. I am truly suprised as when I initially looked at this graph I assumed it would have the most news outlets as this is a place I typically associate with news. However now thinking about it and relating this to my community I really only hear local news from New York about the weather and at times my mom watches morning talk shows that air in New York. I associate California more with celebirty gossip and entertainment news.  I beleive that the high celibrity prescense and movie and tv production in CA has a lot to do with the amount of news outlets that they have in comparrison to NY.
What's the news on the U.S.'s news?
